record.notes: Announced by the IT minister in January 2025; the November 2025 India AI Governance Guidelines call it recently established and propose testing and evaluation of AI systems for risks. The 9 May date concerns a call for partner institutions, not a verified designation date. The exact founding date remains unknown. Not a member of the international network. Projects funded under the IndiaAI Mission's safe and trusted AI pillar are mission grants, not output credited to the institute. A Hindustan Times explainer of 8 August 2026 says the institute is yet to be formally set up.

testing_capacity.notes: The guidelines' section on the institute is recommendatory ('should'): a published government document setting a future task. The May 2025 call says 'The various IndiaAI Safety Institute Cells will function as decentralised capacity of the IndiaAI Safety Institute, executing the assigned technical mandate', but names no partner and assigns no testing. The institute 'oversees the implementation of projects selected under the two rounds of Expressions of Interest (EoIs) under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar', which is oversight of grant projects, not testing for the institute. India is not a member of the international network, so no joint testing is credited.

model_access.notes: No access event, legal power or agreement providing for access to, or evaluation of, the models of a developer that has a model in Epoch AI's frontier set was found. India has no AI statute; the guidelines leave enforcement with sector regulators ('while sector regulators continue to exercise enforcement powers').

claims.text: IndiaAI invited applications for one contract post of Director of the IndiaAI Safety Institute.
It is tasked by the national AI governance guidelines to test and evaluate AI systems for risks.
Its IndiaAI mandate assigns it research and development on indigenous tools, benchmarks and measurement systems to mitigate AI risks.
The national AI governance guidelines recommend resourcing it to develop draft standards and provide technical guidance to regulators and industry.
The national AI governance guidelines recommend resourcing it to provide technical guidance to regulators.
The national AI governance guidelines say it should advise policymakers and industry actors on AI safety.
The national AI governance guidelines say it should anchor India's participation in global forums such as the International Network of AI Safety Institutes.
The IndiaAI Mission's announcement says it will be set up on a hub and spoke model, with research and academic institutions and private sector partners joining the hub and taking up projects.
Its IndiaAI mandate assigns it leading training and awareness programmes for key stakeholders.
The ministry's release says it is responsible for promoting the safe, secure, inclusive and trustworthy development, deployment and adoption of AI in India.

The government's AI governance guidelines list among its suggested key functions conducting forecasting research on the potential impact of AI and issues in online safety, privacy, data governance, labour and competition.

The IndiaAI Mission's call for partnerships says the institute has been established "to advance science-based and indigenous research on AI governance" and approaches to AI safety relevant to the developing world.

sources.title: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation

excerpts.text: the Mission has instituted the AI Safety Institute (AISI), which provides the critical technical expertise needed to conduct research, develop draft standards, and perform safety testing, ensuring governance is resilient, scientiﬁcally informed, and capable of addressing risks as they emerge.
Safety Institute (AISI)
The recently established AI Safety Institute (AISI) should act as the main body responsible for guiding the safe and trusted development and use of AI in India.

The AISI should be involved in research, risk assessment, and capacity-building. It should test and evaluate AI systems for risks and provide advice to policymakers and industry actors on issues of AI safety.
Develop draft guidelines, codes, standards, respective evaluation metrics and testing frameworks in collaboration with relevant agencies and sectoral regulators.
The AISI should also anchor India’s participation in global forums and facilitate collaborations, such as in the International Network of AI Safety Institutes.

Provide adequate resources to the IndiaAI Safety Institute to conduct research, develop draft standards and their evaluation metrics and testing methods and benchmarks, collaborate with international bodies, national standard making bodies and provide technical guidance to regulators and industry.
Conduct forecasting research on the potential impact of AI and issues in online safety, privacy, data governance, labour, and competition.
